Standardise labels and predicted probabilities

Source: R/inputs.R
label_inputs.Rd

label_inputs() converts the many ways of supplying given labels and out-of-sample predicted probabilities into one validated object. Every other function in labelnoise calls it, so anything accepted here is accepted everywhere:

  • a label vector (factor, character or integer) plus a probability matrix or data frame in pred_probs;

  • a data frame of predictions in the yardstick convention: a truth column and one .pred_<level> column per class (as returned by tune::collect_predictions() or augment());

  • a tune_results object from tune::fit_resamples() or tune::tune_grid() fitted with control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE);

  • an mlr3 PredictionClassif or ResampleResult with predict_type = "prob";

  • a caret train object fitted with classProbs = TRUE and savePredictions = "final" (or "all").

Predicted probabilities must be out-of-sample (for example from cross-validation). In-sample probabilities from a model that has seen the labels will hide most label errors.

When an example has several out-of-sample predictions (repeated cross-validation), its probabilities are averaged.

Other packages can add methods for their own prediction objects. A method should end by calling label_inputs() on a label vector and a probability matrix.

Usage

label_inputs(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'labelnoise_inputs'
label_inputs(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
label_inputs(x, pred_probs, ..., row_id = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
label_inputs(x, truth, ..., pred_probs = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'tune_results'
label_inputs(x, ..., parameters = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'PredictionClassif'
label_inputs(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ResampleResult'
label_inputs(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'train'
label_inputs(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Labels or an object holding labels and predicted probabilities. See Description.

...

Passed on to methods. For data frames, a tidyselect specification of the probability columns.

pred_probs

A numeric matrix or data frame with one row per example and one column per class. Rows must sum to one. Columns are matched to labels by name when both have names, otherwise by position.

row_id

Integer identifiers returned in the .row column of find_label_issues(). Defaults to seq_along(x).

truth

For data frames, the column holding the given labels.

parameters

For tune_results with several candidate models, a one-row data frame of tuning parameters, such as the output of tune::select_best().

Value

An object of class labelnoise_inputs: a list with labels (factor), pred_probs (numeric matrix with one column per level of labels) and row_id (integer).

Examples

labels <- factor(c("a", "b", "b", "a"))
probs <- matrix(
  c(0.9, 0.1,
    0.2, 0.8,
    0.7, 0.3,
    0.6, 0.4),
  ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(NULL, c("a", "b"))
)
label_inputs(labels, probs)
#> <labelnoise_inputs>: 4 examples, 2 classes

# The yardstick convention
preds <- data.frame(class = labels, .pred_a = probs[, 1], .pred_b = probs[, 2])
label_inputs(preds, truth = class)
#> <labelnoise_inputs>: 4 examples, 2 classes
